---
title: "With polars extension (.shz)"
toc: true
---

`shoez` ships an opt-in [polars](https://docs.pola.rs/) accessor for fitting
and applying steps in one expression, without building a `Recipe`. Importing
`shoez.polars` registers a `shz` namespace on polars DataFrames:

```{python}
import polars as pl

import shoez.polars  # registers the `df.shz` accessor
from shoez import Selectors as s
```

Each `df.shz.step_*(...)` call fits the step on `df`, applies it, and returns a
fresh polars DataFrame — so calls chain, and the result is just another polars
frame. It is thin sugar over the recipe lifecycle
(`Recipe(...).fit(df).transform(df)`), and it is the one place `shoez` depends
on polars directly, which is why you opt in with an explicit import.

Every step has a matching `step_*` method whose arguments mirror the step's
constructor. The three below cover the most common feature-engineering jobs;
this small frame gives each one something to do:

```{python}
orders = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "city": ["NYC", "LA", "NYC", "SF", "LA", "SF"],
        "price": [10.0, 20.0, None, 30.0, 25.0, 12.0],
        "qty": [2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 4],
    }
)
orders
```

## Handle missing values: `step_impute_median`

`step_impute_median` fills nulls with the column's median (`step_impute_mean`
and `step_impute_mode` are the other flavors):

```{python}
filled = orders.shz.step_impute_median(s.numeric_features())
filled
```

## Make everything numeric: `step_dummy`

`step_dummy` expands nominal columns into numeric indicator columns, dropping
the first level as the reference:

```{python}
orders.shz.step_dummy(s.nominal())
```

## Multivariate feature engineering: `step_pca`

`step_pca` replaces numeric columns with their projection onto principal
components (here on the imputed frame, since PCA needs complete data):

```{python}
filled.shz.step_pca(s.numeric_features(), num_comp=2)
```

## Beyond these three

Because each call returns a polars frame, the steps compose into a pipeline by
chaining — impute, dummy-encode, then project:

```{python}
(
    orders
    .shz.step_impute_median(s.numeric_features())
    .shz.step_dummy(s.nominal())
    .shz.step_pca(s.numeric_features(), num_comp=2)
)
```

The accessor has a `step_*` method for every public step, plus a generic
`df.shz.apply(*steps)` that runs any `Step` instances in one shot.
